abstract: Lumbar disc degeneration disease (LDDD) is a major structural cause of low back pain, one of the leading causes of disability worldwide, and has no disease-modifying treatment. We performed RNA sequencing of 72 intraoperative intervertebral disc samples from the Russian disc degeneration study (RuDDS) cohort, comparing severe (Pfirrmann grades IV-V) with moderate (grade III) degeneration. We identified 731 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; 347 upregulated and 384 downregulated in severely degenerated discs) in the 57 samples that passed quality control. Upregulated DEGs were enriched for extracellular matrix organisation, ossification, and TGF-beta; and Hippo signalling, whereas downregulated DEGs were enriched for immune and inflammatory processes. We identified five differentially active transcription factors, including the TGF-beta; effectors SMAD3 and SMAD4 and the osteogenic regulator DLX5. Of the five, only DLX5 was also a DEG. DEGs were enriched for LDDD-associated genes from Open Targets (odds ratio = 1.68, P = 3.37 * 10-6). Connectivity mapping against the LINCS L1000 database showed that histone deacetylase inhibitors and glucocorticoids reverse the signature of severe degeneration. Together, these results point to TGF-beta-driven fibrotic and osteogenic remodelling as the dominant transcriptional feature of severe disc degeneration, and prioritise candidate genes and compounds for functional validation.
